  PROBLEM: `threads_by_comment` is built by iterating every `comment_ids` entry across every thread (lines 241-247), so its length is the total number of mapped comment IDs, not the number of distinct threads. The trailing "keyed by comment id" suffix does not correct the misread: a single thread whose anchor plus three replies contributes four keys, but the operator reading the log sees "4 thread(s)" and concludes the PR has four open review threads.
  WHY: when the operator triages a failed run, the diagnostic message inflates thread counts and can hide a real-world case where one heavily-replied thread dominates the queue. This is the only spot in the script that exposes a thread/comment-id count, so the wrong number is what propagates to incident reports and the resolution log.

  PROBLEM: threads_by_comment is built at lines 241-247 with exactly one dict entry per comment id (every anchor and every reply in every thread). Therefore len(threads_by_comment) is a count of comment ids, not threads, but the log line labels it "thread(s)". Whenever a thread contains more than one comment, the emitted count is inflated.
  WHY: This pipeline itself appends rationale replies to ignored threads, so multi-comment threads are the steady-state case, not an edge case. The run log then prints e.g. "7 thread(s) keyed by comment id" for 4 actual threads, misleading anyone triaging resolution behavior. Minimal fix (1 line): reword to "comment id(s) keyed for thread lookup" or count distinct thread_id values. Matches the unaddressed Copilot comment entry[14] at plan.py:252.
